name: Frontal Encephalocele

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence reported in Southeast Asia and parts of Africa

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Encephalocele

criteria.description: Presence of a midline frontal or nasal mass at birth
Neuroimaging (MRI or CT) demonstrating herniation of brain tissue and meninges through a defect in the frontal bone
Associated craniofacial anomalies such as hypertelorism or nasal deformity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a visible frontal mass with confirmatory neuroimaging showing herniation of brain tissue through a frontal bone defect
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

imaging: MRI showing herniation of brain tissue and meninges through frontal bone defect
CT scan demonstrating bony defect in frontal region
Ultrasound prenatal screening may detect encephalocele
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or associated with syndromic conditions
other: Physical examination revealing pulsatile frontal mass

distinguishingFeatures: No communication with intracranial cavity on imaging
Midline nasal or frontal mass without brain tissue herniation
No pulsation or increase in size with crying

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of frontal mass
references: Cohen MM Jr. Craniofacial Anomalies: Diagnosis and Management. Oxford University Press, 2018.
National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD): Encephalocele
